incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: unusual S3 outbound traffic from staging auth-proxy (detected by outbound-egress-monitor). possible debug log dump to s3://redwood-staging-debug-dumps. auto-paging oncall (Ravi).
Alex: seeing spikes in staging, paging Ravi. looks like multiple objects uploaded between 10:23-10:27 UTC.
Ravi: on it — joining. Which cluster/hosts?
Alex: staging cluster-2 (us-west-2), host group staging-kube-nodes-2. bandwidth jump ~8x baseline and ~200MB total to that bucket. sample log lines show svc token ids embedded in debug output.
Nora: any prod traffic implicated?
Alex: quick check: no prod access keys used, flows originate from staging pods only. not sure if any customer PII included yet — logs are debug-level.
Kim: triage plan (high level): 1) isolate staging-kube-nodes-2 from egress to S3 (temporary ACL). 2) rotate all staging service tokens and any staging S3 creds. 3) audit S3 objects, set retention/lock and snapshot. 4) assess PII exposure and notify compliance/legal if needed.
Alex: putting snippet of suspicious lines (redacted):
```
2026-05-01T10:24:11Z auth-proxy DEBUG upload s3://redwood-staging-debug-dumps/debug_dump_01.tar.gz size=52428800 token=svc-token-abc1234 user_id=usr_42 prompt_snippet="order of magnitude..."
2026-05-01T10:25:03Z auth-proxy DEBUG upload s3://redwood-staging-debug-dumps/debug_dump_02.tar.gz size=73400320 token=svc-token-xyz9876 user_id=usr_84 prompt_snippet="confidential: ..."
```
Alex: those token strings are real service tokens for staging services (rotatable).
Ops-bot: runbook: isolated host-group staging-kube-nodes-2 (egress policy applied) — step recorded (runbook:egress-isolate).
Ravi: starting token rotation for svc-token-abc1234 and svc-token-xyz9876. executing rotation script on auth-service. sample commands:
```
# rotate service token (staging only)
./scripts/rotate_token.sh --service auth-service --env staging --old-token svc-token-abc1234
# update k8s secret and restart pods
kubectl -n staging set secret auth-service-creds --from-literal=TOKEN=<new> && kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-service
```
Samira: quick question — any raw user creds or full access tokens in the dumps? we need to know customer impact before we send notifications.
Alex: running a grep across the dumped objects now: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-staging-debug-dumps/ - | tar -tzf - | xargs -n1 aws s3 cp s3://redwood-staging-debug-dumps/` — found 4 objects with prompt snippets and two occurrences of partial session ids, no production API keys. treating snippets as sensitive (could contain PII).
Alex: summary of findings: 4 objects total (debug_dump_01..04.tar.gz), contain prompt snippets with user_ids and trace ids; no prod creds, but two staging service tokens present in logs.
Kim: good work. escalate to incident ticketing: I'll create INC-2026-457 and loop in legal + compliance + infra. severity: Sev2 (potential data exposure, staging only). notify any impacted customers only after legal signoff. :lock:
Nora: handoff — Ravi carries incident through next hour; I'll prepare a post-rotation verification checklist (S3 ACLs, object inventory, confirm deletes + retention).
incident-bot: handoff noted — oncall:Ravi until 2026-05-02T04:00:00Z.
Alex: will prepare deletion manifest and request S3 object deletion after we snapshot and preserve copies for forensic review (S3 inventory + Glacier snapshot). posting manifest when ready.
Ravi: rotation in progress, restarting auth-service pods now. I'll post completion and then run the post-rotation connectivity tests and re-run egress monitor.
Samira: thanks — I’ll stand by for any PII findings to start customer-notify draft.
Alex: next updates in ~15m with rotation+delete status.
Ravi: update at 10:40 UTC — tokens rotated, pods restarted, egress policy still applied. will validate bucket contents next.
